newsitem.title: USA: U.S. East Coast is told to monitor tropical storm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. East Coast is told to monitor tropical storm.

text.p: The third tropical storm of the 1997 Atlantic hurricane season formed off the east coast of the United States on Sunday, a day after the season's first hurricane, Bill, faded in the northern Atlantic.

As of 11 p.m. EDT (0300 GMT Monday), the center of Tropical Storm Claudette was near latitude 32.3 north and longitude 73.3 west, or about 240 miles (386 km) south-southeast of Cape Hatteras, North Carolina, the National Hurricane Center said.
The storm was nearly stationary, but forecasters said they expected it to begin drifting northward Monday.

"Although the forecast track does not show a large threat to land, the motion is uncertain, and interests along the mid-Atlantic (U.S.) coast should monitor the progress of the storm," the National Hurricane Center said in its 11 p.m. update.
Maximum sustained winds were near 45 mph (72 kph), with higher gusts, and some strengthening was expected during the next 24 hours.
Claudette would become a hurricane if its maximum sustained winds reach 74 mph (119 kph).
